person_note: Dominick Birdsey is the controlling participating narrator, and numerous event quotes independently expose his I/my voice. Permissioned opening and interior excerpts sustain that voice, while scholarly and major trade reviews identify him as the narrator across the book. The grandfather's autobiography is a juxtaposed first-person document, so even with more than one narrating voice it does not create a different-person strand. Dialogue, aphorisms, Dr. Patel's q00192 speech, and q00188's localized rhetorical you are not evidence of second-person base narration. No credible contrary person evidence remained.
